subject: storytime
title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
about: Aesop's fable of the ants who work all summer and the grasshopper who sings and plays, told gently: when winter comes the ants share their food, and the grasshopper learns to work and plan ahead. First graders know the pull between playing now and getting ready for later, which makes this an easy lesson to talk about. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, four pages long.
tip: Ask: what is one thing you can do today to be ready for tomorrow, like packing your school bag?

book.author: Aesop (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A busy ant, a singing grasshopper, and a long, cold winter.

passage.text:
It was a warm summer day.
A grasshopper hopped in the grass.
He sang and sang.
"La, la, la!"
An ant went by.
She had a big seed on her back.
"Come and play!" said the grasshopper.
"I can't," said the ant.
"I have work to do."
"I am saving food for the winter."
***
"Winter is a long way off," said the grasshopper.
And he sang some more.
Day after day, the ants worked.
They carried seeds and corn to their nest.
Day after day, the grasshopper played.
"Come and play!" he said.
"We have work to do," said the ants.
The grasshopper just laughed.
***
Then the days got short and cold.
Snow fell on the grass.
The grasshopper was cold and hungry.
He looked for food, but there was none.
He went to see the ants.
Knock, knock!
"Please help me," he said.
"I have no food, and I am so cold."
***
The ants had lots of food.
"Come in," they said.
"We will share with you."
They gave him seeds and corn.
Soon he was warm and full.
"Thank you," said the grasshopper.
"Next summer, I will work, too."
And he did!
He still sang, but he worked, too.
It is smart to work and plan ahead.

cards.q: Who sang and played in the grass?
cards.note: A grasshopper is a green or brown bug with long back legs, made for hopping.

cards.q: What did the ant have on her back?
cards.note: Real ants can carry things much heavier than their own bodies.

cards.q: What were the ants saving food for?
cards.note: In winter there is snow and no food to find, so the ants fill their nest while it is warm.

cards.q: Where did the grasshopper go when snow fell?
cards.note: He knocked and asked the ants for help, even though he had laughed at their work.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: Summer comes first in this story, then winter, so ask him what the grasshopper did all summer.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: In the oldest tellings the ants send him away, but here they share and he learns to work.

cards.q: How did the grasshopper feel when the ants shared?
cards.note: He said thank you, so ask him how it feels when someone shares with him.
The ants worked while it was warm, so they had enough to share when it got cold.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'plan ahead' mean?
cards.note: The ants planned ahead when they saved food in the summer for the cold winter.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
